I give up. I read the statement and I don't have a proof I can formalize in this setting.

The statement is not trivially true. `P` must have type `Polynomial ℤ`, since `P = Q * R` with `Q R : Polynomial ℤ`, and the solution is `True`. So the goal is the real content of Putnam 2021 A6: if a 0/1-coefficient polynomial factors into nonconstant integer polynomials, then `P(2)` is composite.

Two of the three conjuncts are routine: `P(2) > 0` because the coefficients are nonnegative and `P ≠ 0`, and `P(2) ≠ 1` because otherwise `P` would be constant. The non-primality is the hard part. The standard argument needs an analytic bound on the roots of 0/1 polynomials (a Mahler-measure-type estimate) to show that a prime value forces one factor to be ±1 at `2`, which is a contradiction. Mathlib has no ready-made tool for that, and I didn't have a route to build it in this session.

I did not modify `/work/putnam_2021_a6.lean`, so the `sorry` remains.
